title: Living with the end of water fluoridation: a qualitative study of families, dental teams and councillors in a coastal town
abstract: Objective: to understand how families and local professionals understand and respond to the end of community water fluoridation, and what shapes their trust. Design: qualitative study with about 40 interviews and four role-specific focus groups, purposively sampled towards families in the most deprived neighbourhoods. Analysis: reflexive thematic analysis. Findings will follow fieldwork.
introduction: Comparative studies suggest that decay rises after fluoridation stops, most in deprived children, but no study has asked families after cessation what they know and do. Consultations about fluoridation are dominated by organised groups.
methods: Participants are recruited through children's centres, school nurses, dental practices and both campaign groups, with interpreters and vouchers. Interviews and focus groups are analysed with reflexive thematic analysis by two analysts.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present themes on understanding, actions and trust, compared by deprivation and role.
discussion: The discussion will relate the themes to the council's 2027 consultation and to advice from dental teams, and will re-examine the sampling rationale in light of the corrected parent survey.
limitations: One town; views may shift over time; one cited source was corrected after the design was accepted.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim that cessation caused more decay.
summary: COREQ and SRQR structured draft with findings left empty.
